summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 68.2 (SDK-owned read chain + resolved folder listings) of CipherBox via GSD workflow (plan-phase → execute-phase), then close out any verification gaps including a full local web-e2e re-confirmation, while also spinning up a parallel worktree for Phase 69.
summary.outcome: All 16 plans across the phase (12 original + 2 gap-closure for SC#5 desync + 2 gap-closure for two newly-discovered file-browser regressions) were implemented, independently verified, and committed; the SC#5 desync bug, an isFileRef download-affordance regression, and a post-upload subfolder-refresh regression were all found and fixed; batch-download, shared-folder-desync, and writable-shares specs pass fully on a fresh e2e stack, leaving only CI re-confirmation as the final open item.

repo: GSD commit-helper (`gsd-tools query commit`) frequently reports `commit_failed` as a false negative even when the commit lands cleanly — always verify with `git log` before retrying or panicking.

In this pnpm monorepo, worktree-based parallel executors are expensive (separate `pnpm install` per worktree) and most waves are single-plan, so sequential execution on the main tree is preferred over worktree parallelism for execute-phase.

`worktree.baseRef` config determines whether executor worktrees fork from `origin/main` (missing local planning commits) or live HEAD (`"head"` — carries all PLAN.md files); must be checked before dispatching worktree executors.
Web app has no dedicated `typecheck` npm script; typecheck must be run via `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.build.json` directly (or `tsc -b`).

Kubo/IPFS version is consistently pinned to v0.42.0 across all tracked docker-compose files and CI configs; a stray `byo-ipfs-kubo` standalone container (v0.40.0, not in any compose file) and a stale `.planning/codebase/INTEGRATIONS.md` doc were the only actual drift.

Web-e2e stack (`cipherbox-infrastructure` docker-compose project) can persist across sessions (was up 5 days), which confounds 'stack flake vs real regression' triage — must recreate fresh (`down -v --remove-orphans` + `up -d`) to get an authoritative read, scoped only to that compose project so unrelated `irl-network-*`/`byo-ipfs-kubo` containers aren't touched.
`.env` files are blocked from reading (contain secrets like TEST_LOGIN_SECRET, DB_PASSWORD) — identify stack composition via docker container names + compose files instead.

gsd plan-checker and gsd-verifier subagents independently re-run tests/greps against actual code rather than trusting executor self-reports — this caught real gaps (SC#5 not actually fixed by plan 12) that grep-based acceptance criteria missed.

code.finding: isFileRef(item) returns `item.kind === 'file'` — for a bare SealedChildRef (no kind field, post kind-cache deletion in plan 11) this always evaluates false, silently breaking any caller that hadn't been migrated to pass a ResolvedChild.

Post-upload refresh (`handleSync`) called `client.listFolder(rootIpnsName)` without `{forceResolve:true}` and also always refreshed the root folder — even when the upload happened in a subfolder, so uploaded files never appeared in the current view.

`onUploadComplete` handler only called `handleSync` (root refresh); needed `invalidateOpenFolder()` added to force-refresh the actually-open (possibly subfolder) view immediately after upload rather than waiting for the 30s poll tick.

ensureFolderLoaded short-circuited on cached folderTree entries and never re-resolved IPNS on repeat navigation — root cause of the SC#5 desync bug; fixed in gap-closure plan 13 via a gated `forceResolve` option routed through enforceResolved.
reresolveInFlight dedup map added in plan 13 to prevent redundant concurrent re-resolves when forceResolve is used from multiple freshness triggers (nav, poll, post-mutation).

workflow: When a background/subagent stalls mid-stream (API Error: Response stalled), check disk/git state directly before re-spawning — it may have made partial progress or none at all; here the planner did zero file writes despite 17 tool calls, so re-authoring the plans directly (with full context already gathered) was faster than re-running a 12-min subagent.

A subagent that sets up Monitors and yields repeatedly on background events without delivering the requested result should be stopped (TaskStop) and the orchestrator should take direct control rather than continuing to resume it.

ScheduleWakeup delay computations can go stale if there's a gap (e.g. hitting a quota limit) between computing the delay and calling the tool — always re-fetch current time immediately before scheduling.

When triaging suspected flaky e2e failures, refute the 'stack degradation' hypothesis by reproducing on a genuinely fresh stack before accepting it — here it revealed two real regressions that would otherwise have been dismissed as flake.

Spot-checking every executor's output independently (re-running tests, re-reading gate results) rather than trusting SUMMARY self-reports caught premature requirement completion marks (SDK-READ-01/02 marked [x] before their deletion ACs were actually met) multiple times.

friction: Planner subagent stalled mid-stream after 12 minutes and 17 tool calls without producing any plan files, wasting the full run.

e2e verification subagent got stuck in a yield-loop, repeatedly reporting interim Monitor events without ever delivering the priority result (desync spec outcome), requiring manual TaskStop and direct orchestrator takeover.
zsh glob expansion (`grep --include=*.ts`) repeatedly failed with 'no match' errors, requiring fallback to `git grep` or exact paths.
ScheduleWakeup was miscalculated once (used a stale timestamp from before a quota-reset gap), landing 25 minutes later than intended (04:35 vs 4:10am) until corrected.

Multiple docker stacks with overlapping ports/services (kubo v0.42.0 vs v0.40.0, postgres :5432 vs :5433) made it easy to misattribute environment issues; had to carefully verify container ownership before any destructive `down -v`.

Initial diagnosis of Regression B (stale cache) was correct but incomplete — the actual root cause (wrong-folder refresh, not just missing forceResolve) only surfaced after the first fix still failed the writable-shares spec, costing an extra investigation + fix round-trip.

Long-running local e2e stack (5 days uptime) initially made regression triage ambiguous between real bugs and stack-degradation flake, requiring a full fresh-stack recreation to get a trustworthy signal.
open_items: CI-based web-e2e re-confirmation is still pending (VERIFICATION.md / UAT.md status) — project doctrine treats CI fresh-container runs as authoritative over local runs.
Fresh e2e stack (docker cipherbox-infrastructure + background API dev server) was left running for verification and needs teardown after final close-out.
Phase 68.2 final close-out (marking phase complete vs. leaving UAT open pending CI) had not been finalized at the end of the transcript.

Phase 69 planning/execution in the separate worktree (/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box-phase69) is independently in progress in another session and should mirror 68.2's SDK-owned read-chain design once available.

The other 13 web-e2e failures classified as pre-existing 68.1 debt (GAP-1 AEAD/streaming, GAP-2 cold-reload DFS, recovery v2-blob env) remain unfixed and tracked separately, not part of this phase's scope.
